subject: Clarify how prefix reuse & KV cache affect billable units — invoice mapping proposal

Subject: Clarify billing for reused prompt prefixes / KV cache

Hi Sergio —

Quick follow-up from procurement after we reviewed the SOW: we need a clear, line-item explanation for how prefix reuse is billed. Our engineers reuse a ~3k token prefix (legal + product context) across tens of thousands of short calls; they expect that since Redwood caches the KV for the prefix, we should not be billed repeatedly for those same prefix tokens at full rate. Procurement scoped this as a billing policy question: do cached prefixes consume billable tokens per call, are they deduplicated within an invoice window, and how do minimums/quantum rounding apply when the live request payload is below the per-call minimum?

Can you send a simple calculation example (3 scenarios) and a proposed invoice mapping we can include in the SOW? Also flag any limits (ttl, cross-session reuse, region constraints).

Thanks — Emma
Emma Lowe

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: Redwood charges for tokens that contribute to model compute when requests are executed; KV cache prefix reuse reduces compute but does not always remove billing for the prefix automatically, depending on cache hit semantics and invoice windowing.

I'm pulling together a short worked example and a proposed invoice mapping to include in the SOW (three scenarios: same-session reuse, cached prefix reused across requests inside invoice window, and cross-day reuse where cache TTL expired). I also want to confirm whether Novus would prefer a per-invoice credit for deduplicated prefix tokens vs. an ongoing discounted per-token rule for that prefix.

I'll loop in Karthik and Priyom for exact math and a formal term you can accept. Expect a doc + CSV sample by EOD.

Best,
Sergio

Team — forwarding Novus ask. They want a clear, auditable example and a recommended invoicing mapping to include in SOW ND-2029-042. Key constraints: prefix ~3k tokens, average live request 120 tokens, ~50k calls per day from the same app. Their procurement prefers a one-line billing treatment in SOW rather than bespoke monthly credits.

Questions:
- Can we offer a per-invoice dedup credit for prefix tokens when a cache hit is observed >= 95% of calls in an invoice window?
- If we do per-invoice dedup credits, what's a defensible detection window (rolling 24h or invoice-period) and evidence (audit logs showing cache hit ids)?
- How do minimum per-call floors interact (we have a 100-token billing quantum for this account in pilot pricing) — if live request is 120 tokens and the prefix is cached, do we still apply the 100-token floor?

Please propose wording that is tight enough for legal but flexible operationally. Priyom/Karthik, can you prepare: 1) worked numeric examples, 2) suggested SOW clause, 3) a CSV we can attach.

Thanks — Sergio

Subject: Re: FW: Clarify billing for reused prompt prefixes / KV cache

SG — draft numbers below (high-level; attached CSV has row-level calc). Assumptions: prefix 3000 tokens, live payload 120 tokens, per-call quantum = 100 tokens (account pilot), invoice window = monthly (30d), cache TTL = 48h for prefix entries, cache-hit detection via prefix-hash match and KV id.

Scenario A — Same-session reuse (no TTL eviction):
- First call: bill prefix (3,000) + payload (120) -> charged tokens = 3,120 -> quantum rounding = ceil(3120/100)*100 = 3,200 tokens
- Subsequent calls within session (cache hit): runtime compute only for payload (120) -> charged tokens per call = 120 -> rounded = 200 tokens (due to 100-token quantum)
- Effective average per call across N calls (large N) ~ (3,200 + (N-1)*200)/N -> quickly dominated by 200 once N is large.

Scenario B — Cross-request cached reuse within invoice window (cache hit often, dedup credit applied):
- Proposal: for invoice-level dedup, treat the first observed prefix charge in invoice as billable and mark subsequent detected matches as "deduplicated" for billing (credit applied) if hit rate >= 95% for the invoice.
- Example: 50k calls/day, month ~ 1.5M calls. First call charged 3,200 (rounded). Remaining 1,499,999 calls get payload-charge rounded to 200 unless we apply per-invoice dedup credit. If dedup credit applied, we issue a single-line credit equivalent to (prefix_token_charge - payload_equivalent) * (observed_hit_count - 1) (see CSV). This yields a large credit and simplifies per-call line items.

Scenario C — Cache TTL expired or cross-region misses:
- If TTL expired (48h) or request served from a different regional cache without a shared KV id, prefix will be billed again on first miss. We recommend limiting cross-region dedup guarantees; SOW should call out region-bounded dedup and TTL.

Minimum/quantum interaction:
- Quantum floors still apply to final billed token line items. That means even when payload-only compute happens, per-call rounding may make the effective billed tokens larger than raw payload. A per-invoice dedup credit offsets the prefix portion but doesn't change per-call quantum rounding on each line item unless we also agree to a per-call floor override (we can offer that as an add-on).

Suggested SOW clause (draft):
"Redwood Billing: Prefix Deduplication & KV Cache — Redwood will attempt to detect repeated prompt prefixes via prefix-hash and KV-cache identifiers. When the same prefix is observed for >=95% of an account's calls within an invoice period, Redwood will apply an invoice-level credit equal to the sum of redundant prefix charges for the period, subject to cache TTL (48 hours) and region-bound cache scoping. Per-call billing quanta remain in effect; credits will be reflected as separate line items on the invoice."

Attaching CSV and a short doc with example calculations. Happy to tune thresholds.

— Priyom

Subject: Re: Clarify billing for reused prompt prefixes / KV cache

Emma —

Per our internal math (attached CSV), here's a concise mapping we propose for inclusion in the SOW/statement of work:

1) Definition: "Prefix" = any prompt material deterministically hashed and stored in Redwood KV cache; "Cache-hit" = prefix-hash with matching KV id returned at request time.

2) Billing rule: The first observed prefix use in an invoice period will include the full prefix compute charge (rounded by account quantum). Subsequent requests that return a cache-hit are charged for live payload compute only.

3) Invoice-level dedup credit: If cache-hit rate for that prefix >=95% across the invoice period, Redwood will issue a single-line credit equal to the sum of redundant prefix charges (rounded) for the period. Credits exclude calls served from regional caches or where TTL has expired.

4) Quantum/flooring: Account-level billing quantum (100 tokens) applies to all line items. The credit calculation recognizes quantum rounding on the original prefix-charge line.

5) Evidence & audit: Redwood will include cache-hit metrics (prefix-hash, hit-counts) as an attachment to invoice and retain logs for 120 days for audit.

If this is acceptable we can add the paragraph to the SOW and produce a one-page annex with the worked numbers (we attached an example CSV). Let me know if procurement needs per-call floor overrides rather than invoice credits — we can price that as an optional rider.

Thanks,
Sergio
